blocks.h2: Signs Your Sump Pump Needs Attention
blocks.intro: Don't wait for the next storm to find out:

tiles.body: Pour a bucket of water in the pit. If the pump doesn't start, the float or motor has failed.
A stuck float, a failed check valve or a pump too small for the water coming in.
Worn bearings or debris in the impeller. The motor is on its way out.
Even a quiet pump wears out. Most last about that long, less if they run often.

blocks.h2: Sump Pumps in Arlington Heights Basements
blocks.intro: Heavy spring rain, snowmelt and summer storms put sump pumps across the area to the test. The July 2011 storm dropped almost 7 inches in just over three hours.

items.body: The storms that fill your pit are the same ones that take down power lines. A battery backup pump keeps running when the main pump can't.
Many homes from the 1950s and 1960s got a sump pit added later. If you've finished the basement since, the pump and pit may be too small for the job.
A discharge line that's buried shallow or runs flat across the yard can freeze in January. We route it so it drains and add a freeze guard where needed.
A pump tied into the sanitary sewer adds storm water to the line that can back up into your basement. We make sure yours discharges outdoors.

blocks.h2: Sump Pump Questions From Arlington Heights Homeowners

items.q: How often should I replace my sump pump?
items.preview: Every 7 to 10 years for most homes, sooner if it runs a lot.
items.answer: Most sump pumps last somewhere around 7 to 10 years, and less if they run often. Test yours before spring: pour a bucket of water in the pit and watch it turn on and shut off.

items.q: Do I need a battery backup sump pump?
items.preview: If you have a finished basement or anything valuable down there, yes.
items.answer: If your basement is finished or you store anything you care about down there, yes. Power outages and heavy rain tend to happen together, and a backup keeps pumping when the main pump can't.

items.q: Why does my sump pump run when it hasn't rained?
items.preview: High groundwater, a stuck float or water cycling back through a bad check valve.
items.answer: Groundwater can stay high for days after a storm or during snowmelt. If it runs constantly in dry weather, the float may be stuck or the check valve may be letting water fall back into the pit.

items.q: Where should my sump pump discharge?
items.preview: Outside, well away from the foundation.
items.answer: Outside, onto your yard or into a storm drain line, far enough from the house that it doesn't soak back in. It should never go into the sanitary sewer.

items.q: Can my sump pump discharge into the floor drain?
items.answer: No. Sending sump water into the floor drain adds storm water to the sewer, which is exactly what backs up in heavy rain. We'll reroute it outside.

items.q: How much does sump pump replacement cost in Arlington Heights?
items.preview: It depends on the pump, pit and backup. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the pump, whether the pit or check valve needs work and whether you add a backup. We give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.
